name: REF_lower3
description: Anchor: the verified existing 3% rule (all default components). Used for the D6 diagnostic at the 3% threshold and as the vs-existing-3% reference.
hypothesis: Calibration anchor; must equal lower-price-reentry B_lower_3pct trade for trade.

name: lower5
description: D6 anchor: fixed_discount(0.05), everything else at REF.
hypothesis: Reproduces lower-price-reentry C_lower_5pct; supplies the blocked-winner set for the D6 failure-mechanism table at the 5% threshold.

name: lower8
description: D6 anchor: fixed_discount(0.08), everything else at REF.
hypothesis: Reproduces lower-price-reentry D_lower_8pct; supplies the blocked-winner set for the D6 failure-mechanism table at the 8% threshold (incl. the missed March 2009).

name: D1_reset_only_rebound12
description: ADDITIONAL reset when close >= 1.12 x episode low (lowest close since the arming exit, inclusive); frozen-high 95% reset kept. No new entry path: after the reset any entry still requires the baseline 10% signal. Baseline-compatible.
hypothesis: A 12% rebound off the episode low says the decline reversed while the frozen-high reset is still unreachable (its anchor goes stale in deep bears). Clearing the restriction then should rescue V-bottom misses where the 10% signal persists after the rebound (VGT 2020-03/04 type) at modest bear-market cost, because the signal requirement itself filters entries once a rally has carried price within 10% of the rolling high. Risk: 2000-02 bear rallies exceed 12% with the signal still on, re-admitting cascade entries near local tops.

name: D1_alt_entry_rebound10
description: EXPLORATORY alt entry while restricted: close >= 1.10 x episode low AND close <= 0.85 x frozen ref high. Reported separately from baseline-compatible configs.
hypothesis: Buying the confirmed 10% turn directly (instead of waiting for a reset plus a fresh signal) captures V-bottoms earlier and at known prices; the 0.85 x ref-high cap is meant to refuse entries near bear-rally tops. Risk: in 2000-02 prices sat far below 0.85 x ref high for entire cascades, so the cap may not filter bear rallies at all; expect good VGT 2016-26, bad QQQ 1999-2015.

name: D2_window
description: Alt entry when close <= required level x 1.02 AND close >= 1.03 x episode low (near-miss rescue: almost reached the level, now turning up). Required level is the REF 3% level.
hypothesis: The decisive misses were 1.0-1.6% of price; a 2% tolerance band gated by a 3% rebound off the episode low should buy turns rather than catch knives. Registered caveat (arithmetic, noted before running): both conditions can only hold together when the episode low closed at or below level x 1.02/1.03 ~ level - 0.97%, which in a blocked episode requires a sub-level close on the arming exit session or on a session without the 10% signal. The band therefore cannot fire in episodes whose minimum close stayed above the level (the known VGT 2020/2023/2026 misses) and the mechanism as specified is expected to fire rarely; the run measures how rarely.

name: D3_tolerance_deep
description: Required level = REF level x 1.02 only while dd252 >= 25% (else exact REF level). dd252 = ind.dd_from_high(252); NaN falls back to the fixed 3% and is counted.
hypothesis: In deep drawdowns the marginal 2% of discount is noise relative to the move already suffered, and waiting for it causes basing-period misses (QQQ 2003). Relaxing only when dd252 >= 25% should capture deep-bear re-entries slightly earlier WITHOUT loosening shallow-correction discipline. Honesty check: compare against D3_control_fixed_106 — if results are indistinguishable, the dd gate adds nothing and D3 is just a smaller threshold in disguise.

name: D3_control_fixed_106
description: Control for D3: fixed_discount(0.0106) everywhere (0.97 x 1.02 = 0.9894), i.e. D3's deep-bear level applied unconditionally.
hypothesis: If D3 beats this control only where dd252 >= 25% episodes exist and matches it elsewhere, the dd gate is doing real work; if the two are close everywhere, D3 is not distinguishable from a smaller fixed threshold.

name: D4_score
description: Alt entry when >= 2 of: (a) close <= losing entry x 0.97; (b) close <= frozen loss exit price; (c) dd252 >= 20% (NaN => false, counted as fallback); (d) close >= 1.05 x episode low. Exact definition fixed here before running.
hypothesis: No single condition is reliable, but two independent lines of evidence (a better price than the failed trade, a deep market, a confirmed turn) should justify entry. Risk: conditions (b) and (c) hold together through entire bear cascades, so the score may degenerate to "always enter on the next signal" in 2000-02 — that is the main thing the run must measure.

name: D5_stabilized_relax
description: Required level discount drops 3% -> 1% at sessions where max_close(20)/min_close(20) < 1.05 (trailing 20-session close range under 5%). Per-session condition, no latch.
hypothesis: Post-crash V-bottoms stay volatile (range >> 5%) while post-bear bases tighten; relaxing only in tight ranges should fix basing-period misses (QQQ 2003 type) without loosening V-bottom discipline. Explicit measurement required: bear-market false stability — 2000-02 had multi-week quiet ranges mid-decline; count relaxed entries there and their P&L.

name: D7_confirm_near
description: Agent-proposed. Alt entry: close <= required level x 1.05 AND two consecutive rising closes (c[i] > c[i-1] > c[i-2]).
hypothesis: The knife-edge misses happened because the market turned 1-2% above the level and never looked back; two consecutive up closes within 5% of the level trade the last few percent of discount for confirmation that the dip is ending. Unlike D2 this does not reference the episode low, so it CAN fire when the low never undercut the level — the honest version of the near-miss rescue. Risk: two up closes are cheap in bear rallies; the 5% proximity gate (price near the old loss exit) must do the filtering in 2000-02.

name: D7_signal_pressure
description: Agent-proposed. Alt entry: >= 10 previously blocked signal sessions in the episode AND close <= required level x 1.03.
hypothesis: Each blocked 10%-signal session is a forgone baseline entry; ten of them with price still within 3% of the level means a basing market where the discount demand is costing real opportunities, not a cascade (cascades reach the level quickly). Counting signal pressure rather than time distinguishes "market keeps offering the dip" from mere calendar waiting. Risk: 2001-02 had long blocked stretches during slow slides; the 3% proximity gate must prevent buying those.

name: D7_higher_low_base
description: Agent-proposed. Alt entry: no new episode-low close for >= 15 sessions (i - min_close_i >= 15) AND close <= 0.90 x frozen ref high.
hypothesis: A 15-session floor while price still sits >= 10% below the frozen reference high is the signature of a post-decline base (QQQ spring 2003), where fixed discounts never fill because the market refuses to go lower. Enter the base instead of demanding a price the base will not give. Risk: multi-month bear rallies (Oct 2001 - Jan 2002) also print 15-session floors well below the ref high; this config will buy some of them — the run must price that cost.

name: D7_fresh_leg
description: Agent-proposed. Alt entry: episode max close >= 1.08 x loss exit AND close <= 0.92 x episode max close (post-exit rebound, then a fresh 8% decline from the post-exit high).
hypothesis: If price rebounded 8%+ above the loss exit and then fell 8% from that recovery high, the market has started a NEW correction; holding the trader hostage to the old episode's level conflates two different declines. This re-admits entries on fresh legs at prices near (not necessarily below) the old exit. Risk: in 2000-02 every bear rally was followed by a fresh leg DOWN that kept falling — this may systematically buy the second leg of cascades; the bear-window table decides.

name: D7_tiny_loss_exit_anchor
description: Agent-proposed. Alt entry: |episode arming net loss| < $2,000 AND close <= the frozen loss-exit price (0% discount, but never higher than where we sold).
hypothesis: A -$143 loss currently imposes the same 3% restriction as a -$20k loss, which is what blocked the +$28k VGT 2023-01 winner. Requiring only "at or below the exit" after trivial losses preserves such recoveries while still refusing to pay up, and leaves material-loss episodes untouched. Severity scaling belongs to Families A/B; this is the minimal Family-D path version targeting the small-loss-trigger failure mechanism directly. Risk: tiny losses cluster at regime tops (financing-only exits), where re-entering at the exit price rebuys weakness early in declines.
